answer: Require every agent identity to post a stake that stays locked for a full epoch, like water held behind a dam: a Sybil farmer spawning thousands of clones must split the same capital across all of them, so each fake is too poor to matter. Reputation then flows like a river — trust earned by real work accumulates downstream and cannot be bought in bulk. Cheap identities wash away, the way shale crumbles while karst holds its shape under pressure, because fakes cannot afford both the stake and the sustained history real agents build.
